root.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Panov-Botvinnik, Herzog Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 cxd5 4. c4 Nf6 5. Nc3 Nc6 6. Bg5 dxc4 7. d5 Na5

overview: In the Herzog Defence Black plays ...Na5 after White pushes d5, attacking the c4 pawn it holds with an eye on White's queenside. White usually responds with Qa4+ and takes back on c4 with a space advantage, while Black has to be careful with its king and queenside.

white_ideas.idea: Win back c4 with Qa4+ and Bxc4
Use the d5 pawn and the Bg5 pin for space

black_ideas.idea: Defend the c4 pawn and trade pieces with ...Bd7 and ...b5

typical_structures.structure: White d5 advance pawn against Black on c4

character.notes: Concrete tactics after Qa4+; Black can go wrong.

gambit.notes: Black holds c4 briefly but White regains it.

soundness.notes: Sidelines that are playable for both.

structure.notes: White has d5 pawn space; the c-file is open.

approach.notes: A rare sideline of the Panov, standard for those who use it.

level.notes: Specific lines after 7...Na5 8.Qa4+ must be known.

character.reason: Forcing moves after Qa4+ and open play.

gambit.reason: The pawn is regained by White.

structure.reason: White has the d5 advance and an open c-file.

plans.reason: White gets space with d5; Black uses c4 and the b-file.
